stemMd: In the third paragraph, "constrain an interpretation" means

options.label: A
options.textMd: force evidence to match a preferred conclusion.

options.label: B
options.textMd: lengthen a written account without changing its meaning.

options.label: C
options.textMd: make an explanation impossible to revise.

options.label: D
options.textMd: limit the range of plausible explanations.

explanationMd: The team uses independent material to narrow possible vegetation histories. Constrain therefore means to limit which explanations remain plausible.

distractorRationale.c: The research remains open to uncertainty and alternative histories.
distractorRationale.a: The passage describes evidence narrowing conclusions, not manipulating it.
distractorRationale.b: The phrase concerns evidential limits, not word count.
